title: Chicken Paillards with Asparagus, Lemon, Garlic, and Dill
description: A lemony dill sauce brightens chicken breast and complements asparagus. Though there is quite a bit of the herb in here, it does not overwhelm the rest of the dish. Serve with some boiled new potatoes or rice, if you like (in which case you may want to double the sauce, maybe anyway).
ingredients: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves (about 1-3/4 lb.), tenders removed (or thinly sliced chicken breasts)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 large lemon, finely grated to yield 1 tsp. zest and squeezed to yield 3 Tbs. juice
1 lb. asparagus, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
2 Tbs. chopped fresh dill (maybe with some tarragon)
2 Tbs. unsalted butter, cut into 3 or 4 pieces
directions: Using a meat mallet, pound each chicken breast between 2 sheets of plastic wrap to an even 1/4- to 1/2-inch thickness. (Or use, thinly sliced chicken breasts.)
In a shallow bowl, combine the flour, 2 tsp. salt, and 1 tsp. pepper.

Heat 2 Tbs. of the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Dredge 2 paillards in the flour, shaking off any excess, and place in the skillet. Cook, flipping once, until lightly browned, about 4 minutes total. Transfer the chicken to a plate; set aside. Repeat with the remaining oil and paillards.

Add the garlic to the skillet and cook over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, for about a minute. Deglaze the pan with a little wine and add the chicken broth and lemon zest, scraping up any browned bits from the skillet. Add the asparagus, chicken, and any accumulated juice and nestle the chicken into the liquid. Bring to a boil, turn the heat down to maintain a simmer, cover, and cook until the chicken is cooked through and the asparagus is tender, 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer the chicken to a platter or plates.
Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the lemon juice, dill, and butter. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Spoon the asparagus mixture over the chicken and serve.
